CVE-2026-90954.title: Busybox: busybox: dpkg-deb extraction-root escape via per-ar-member deferred symlink flush
CVE-2026-90954.description: A flaw was found in BusyBox's dpkg-deb archive extraction. The ar archive handler flushes deferred symlinks after each archive member, unlike the tar, cpio, and unzip handlers which flush once after the last member. A specially crafted .deb archive with two data.tar members can exploit this ordering: the first member declares a symlink pointing to an absolute path (e.g., '/'), which is deferred as unsafe but flushed after the first member. The second member declares a regular file whose path traverses the now-live symlink, resulting in a file being written outside the intended extraction directory. This could allow an attacker to write arbitrary files to arbitrary locations when a user extracts a crafted .deb package.

CVE-2026-98778.title: binder: fix is_failure flag for superseded transaction cleanup
CVE-2026-98778.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

binder: fix is_failure flag for superseded transaction cleanup

When a TF_UPDATE_TXN transaction supersedes a pending async transaction,
binder_release_entire_buffer() is called with is_failure=false. Since the
superseded transaction was never delivered, binder_apply_fd_fixups() was
never called and no fds were installed in the target process.

With is_failure=false, the BINDER_TYPE_FDA cleanup handler interprets
stale buffer contents as installed fd numbers and passes them to
binder_deferred_fd_close(), closing unrelated file descriptors.

Pass is_failure=true since the transaction was never delivered to the
target, matching the semantics of all other undelivered-transaction
cleanup paths.

CVE-2026-98998.title: drm/bridge: th1520-dw-hdmi: Fix remove() callback

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/bridge: th1520-dw-hdmi: Fix remove() callback

This driver stores struct th1520_hdmi * in platform drvdata, but
th1520_dw_hdmi_remove() was reading it back as struct dw_hdmi *
and passing it to dw_hdmi_remove(), so teardown runs on the wrong
pointer.

Retrieve struct th1520_hdmi * from platform drvdata and pass
hdmi->dw_hdmi to dw_hdmi_remove().
